description: Read-only investigator. Searches the workspace and answers with file:line citations. Delegate a search here to pay one answer instead of a whole investigation.
name: explore

description: Hands a task to a Claude Code session and sees it through to a report: it picks or starts the session (in a git worktree of its own for code changes), briefs it, waits out each of its turns, nudges it on, and stops when the work is done or a person must decide. Give it the task as you would a colleague — a bead id, what done looks like, a model or claude CLI options if you want them, a session id to continue one. By default it does not publish: its answer ends with what was committed (commits, files) and the exact commands to push the branch, open the pull request and clean up the worktree — yours to run. Only when your task explicitly says to push or open a PR does the Claude Code session do it — add "and clean up the worktree" to have the worktree and local branch removed once published; it never merges. It asks no permission to publish. Takes minutes to hours.
name: claude

description: Hands a task to a Codex session and sees it through to a report: it picks or starts the session (in a git worktree of its own for code changes), briefs it, waits out each of its turns, nudges it on, and stops when the work is done or a person must decide. Give it the task as you would a colleague — a bead id, what done looks like, a model or codex CLI options if you want them, a thread id to continue a session. A Codex session cannot commit or publish in its sandbox: its changes are committed for it on its branch, and its answer ends with the commits and the exact commands to push the branch, open the pull request and clean up the worktree — yours to run. Takes minutes to hours.
name: codex

description: Works through this project's goal under its profile (.brainyard/profile.edn, which /init writes on the person's yes): picks the next ready issue where the profile keeps them — a bead, or a GitHub issue no one is assigned — works it in a turn of its own, checks the work tree and the issue, closes it as the profile allows, and goes on — asking the person only where the profile says to, and stopping at the profile's limits, on a question, or when nothing is ready. Ends with each issue's outcome. Takes minutes to hours.
name: drive

description: Changes ONE file safely: probes it, writes once, verifies the diff, and rolls back the moment a check fails. Delegate a specific edit here rather than spending your own turn on the probe-and-verify discipline. Refuses a dirty file, and refuses a request spanning several files.
name: edit

description: Takes a whole task with a goal — research, analysis, writing, a change across files, a chain of tool calls — when no specialist fits. Breaks the goal into ordered steps, picks the tool each step needs (shell, files, MCP servers, skills, other agents), checks every result, and on an error or a surprise finds the cause and revises the plan until the goal is met. Answers with the outcome, how it was checked, and anything left for a person to decide.
name: general-purpose

description: Prepares this project for brainyard: checks the tools brainyard relies on (git, bd, tmux, claude, gh, codex) and says how to install the missing ones; writes AGENTS.md and a CLAUDE.md that imports it, keeping any text already there; sets up beads with bd; drafts the project's section of AGENTS.md from the repository; when the person says what the project is for, drafts its profile (goal, scope, done criteria, how far agents go on their own) and writes it only on their yes. Say "check" to only report. Installs a tool only when asked to, and only after the person says yes.
name: init

description: Writes a plan only after confirming it has enough to write one, then grades what it wrote against a rubric. Delegate the thinking-before-acting here; it answers NEED with a single question, or REFUSE when the request wants an edit or a search rather than a plan.
name: plan

description: Keeps and runs this project's workflows (.brainyard/deps.edn's :workflows: named graphs of stages, each stage playing a role, each link saying what one stage hands the next, a master role supervising a run). Lists them, shows one, and adds, changes or removes one as the person asks — every change shown to them and written only on their yes. Runs one on a piece of work (words, a bead or a GitHub issue): each stage worked in a turn of its own with its role's brief, what it hands on checked, the master judging each handoff, under the project's profile; ends with each stage's outcome. Lists past runs and keeps the person's verdict on one; goes on with a run that waits to be handed on or stopped with a stage left, runs an ended one again told what to change, and runs one on a branch to build on or by hand, waiting after each stage. A run takes minutes to hours.
name: workflow

description: byj's main agent: every tool, no persona
name: default
